items.statement: The half-grid cosine frame has orthogonal columns with squared norm d, zero weighted Gram at frequency2q+1, and row sum of squares at most2(q+1). T^{\top}T=dI_r,\qquad T^{\top}D_{2q+1}T=0,\qquad\sum_{k=0}^{q}T_{ik}^{2}\le2r,\quad r=q+1. \(d,q\) are natural numbers with \(2q+1<d\). This includes \(q=0\) and implies \(d\ge2\). For zero-based \(i=0,\ldots,d-1\), put \(\theta_i=(i+1/2)\pi/d\). The frame has \(r=q+1\) columns: \(T_{i0}=1\) and \(T_{ik}=\sqrt2\cos(k\theta_i)\) for \(1\le k\le q\). \(D_{2q+1}=\operatorname{diag}(\cos((2q+1)\theta_i))\). Transpose, matrix multiplication and row sum of squares are real Euclidean operations. In the private application, \(\mu=N(0,I_{d r})\) is the actual centered Gaussian on coordinates \((i,a)\), and \(B(x)_{i,(a,b)}=d^{-1/2}x_{(i,a)}T_{ib}\). Its moments and Gram-entry integrability are conclusions derived internally.
assumptions: \(d,q\) are natural numbers with \(2q+1<d\). This includes \(q=0\) and implies \(d\ge2\).
For zero-based \(i=0,\ldots,d-1\), put \(\theta_i=(i+1/2)\pi/d\). The frame has \(r=q+1\) columns: \(T_{i0}=1\) and \(T_{ik}=\sqrt2\cos(k\theta_i)\) for \(1\le k\le q\).
\(D_{2q+1}=\operatorname{diag}(\cos((2q+1)\theta_i))\). Transpose, matrix multiplication and row sum of squares are real Euclidean operations.

In the private application, \(\mu=N(0,I_{d r})\) is the actual centered Gaussian on coordinates \((i,a)\), and \(B(x)_{i,(a,b)}=d^{-1/2}x_{(i,a)}T_{ib}\). Its moments and Gram-entry integrability are conclusions derived internally.
